correctness.rationale: PASS: In the actual analytic derivation, two unitary changes yield the exact selfadjoint truncated Hankel kernel. The Taylor expansion has a uniform O(alpha^-2) Hilbert–Schmidt remainder by explicit logarithmic differentiation on u+v<=alpha/2 and exponential tail control. The polynomial identity splits the first-order correction into a changed rank-one positive mode minus an orthogonal negative mode of squared norm 1/8. Min–max and best-rank inequalities give sharp s2=1/(8alpha)+O(alpha^-2) and the rank-two Eckart–Young tail O(alpha^-4). The exact Hilbert–Schmidt mass 1/(4-2/alpha) then yields the 1/32 norm coefficient by algebra. Five finite Nyström spectral checks corroborate but are not used as infinite proofs. Limit alpha→+infinity, alpha real >1, normalization and singular-index quantifiers are explicit.

value.rationale: PASS: The classical Volterra power sequence has long served as a sharp example of spectral concentration; the exact speed and shape of collapse beyond its principal rank-one mode is an intrinsic spectral problem. The coefficient 1/8 identifies the first neglected singular mode, while an O(alpha^-4) squared tail makes a quantitative rank-two approximation available and forces an exact higher-order norm term. These are motivated invariant limits across every large real fractional order, not an arbitrary finite census, tiny isolated numerical gain, or restatement of the known leading norm.
